label: Rewarded D1 late in the episode (trial >= ~70)
explanation: Fires only at D1 and only when the reward input is 1: 100% of activations are at rewarded D1 steps, never at GO, D2, unrewarded D1 or penalties. Within rewarded D1 it is gated by episode progress. The rate is near 0 for trials 0-60, then jumps to 12-16% of all steps over trials 70-99, and 91% of mass falls in trials 50-99. The model value head says the same thing: activity is confined to low-value steps (value < 7.13, about 0 above 8.1). Value probably falls late in the episode because fewer trials remain, so the two are near-equivalent proxies. The value-based predicate scores slightly better on dev (F1 0.72, mass recall 0.84 vs F1 0.72, mass recall 0.77); I recorded ep_trial for interpretability. Both use only observed or internal variables, no future ones. Reward-prediction history (common/rare, stay) modulates the rate only weakly (e.g. prev_common rare 0.7x). The missed activations are weak firings on rewarded D1 steps before trial 70. False positives are rewarded late D1 steps where it stays silent, so precision is ~0.63. This is likely a slow episode-time / low-value signal, read out on rewarded D1.
